claims.text: Pre-coating tungsten particles with a thin, conformal Cu layer by ALD before SPS will improve W–Cu interfacial contact relative to SPS of uncoated powders.
ALD Cu pre-coating before SPS will eliminate interfacial void formation.
Improved W–Cu contact and reduced void formation will enhance thermal transport.
ALD-assisted SPS will improve mechanical durability under fusion-reactor irradiation conditions relative to conventional SPS without ALD.
W–Cu materials prepared by SPS or similar powder-consolidation routes typically exhibit phase separation and interfacial voids.
A sub-micron, uniform Cu coating can be deposited on W particles through ALD.
The proposed SPS processing range is approximately 1100–1200 °C in vacuum or an inert atmosphere.
The proposed service test range is 600–800 °C with thermal cycling and mechanical loading representative of fusion-reactor joints.
The ALD Cu coating will produce a defect-minimized W–Cu interface.
The ALD Cu coating will enhance atomic diffusion during SPS sufficiently to fully bond the W and Cu phases.
A conformal ALD Cu layer promotes better wetting during SPS.
A conformal ALD Cu layer promotes W–Cu interdiffusion during SPS.
Improved wetting and interdiffusion reduce or eliminate interfacial voids and phase separation.
Interfacial voids and phase separation impair thermal conductivity and mechanical integrity under irradiation and thermal cycling.
The ALD-coated composite will have fewer voids and stronger interfacial bonding than an uncoated SPS composite.
The ALD-coated composite will have higher thermal conductivity than an uncoated SPS composite.
The ALD-coated composite will have greater mechanical durability than an uncoated SPS composite.
Conventional SPS or mechanical alloying of uncoated W and Cu powders tends to produce defects and voids that degrade thermal transport and mechanical properties.
ALD coating thickness and uniformity must be optimized to avoid introducing additional phases.
